Jack Fletcher sends us a long and interesting letter from India. Beginning with reminiscences of running and socials, he then reviews his career in the Services.
Regretfully we have to record the death of Len Fletcher, after a long illness, at the early age of 54 years. Our sincere condolences are extended to Mrs.

Go to a fixture on the Brighton Road and the chances are that you will bump into JACK "NOBBY" FLETCHER. For many years he was a member of our cross-country packs and has probably seen more "Brightons" than any other member.

We are sorry to learn that Jack "Nobby" Fletcher had a double spell in hospital this summer. He was, however, sufficiently recovered to see this year's Brighton walk and we can be sure that seeing our present walkers repeating our triumphs of earlier days did him much good.

CHARLIE CHURCHER was seen talking to old friends, whilst CHARLIE JONES, FRANK WEBB, NORMAN DEWBERRY and CHARLIE MacLENNAN were about doing various jobs around the course. JACK FLETCHER is obviously fit again and goes for a morning swim at Tooting Bec Open Bath!
We mourn the passing of another loyal Belgravian, Jack ("Nobby") Fletcher who died recently. He joined the Club in the '20s' and was a "regular" both over the country and on the track.

Jack Fletcher, one of our younger runners, pulled us back to fourth and our Running Secretary Ernie Duffett maintained this position over the four and a half mile stretch to Handcross – as did Arthur Penny over stage seven.
